15 - [Negative/CRITICAL] Verify the Invoice tab shows the invoice number and Print options
CONFIRMED REAL CRITICAL DEFECT, found 2026-08-28 (was passing in an earlier session — real regression, not a stale test). Clicking the Invoice tab on an order detail page no longer renders the invoice — it renders a full PHP fatal-error debug page (Spatie/Ignition error handler, via the `Swissup_Ignition` module) instead. Confirmed via direct page-content capture, not a selector guess: the real error is "Call to a member function getOrderType() on null" at app/design/frontend/Kemana/steelhub/Magento_Sales/templates/order/ view.phtml:27. Reproduced on 2 different orders (#000000075/order_id 99, and order_id 98) — systemic, not order-specific. The Shipment/ Dikirim tab has the identical failure (test 16); the Ulasan tab does NOT (confirmed working normally on the same order in the same session) — the bug is scoped to whatever block/data these 2 tabs specifically depend on.
Failed ▼

⚠ ErrorThis test case has been explicitly marked as failed.

🔍 Root Cause
view.phtml:27 calls ->getOrderType() (or similar) on an object that is null at render time — most likely a block/model expected to be pre-loaded with an Invoice (or Shipment) collection/entity isn't being set before the template renders, so a method call on it fails fatally instead of the template defensively checking for null first. Confirmed real via the site's own Ignition debug page (PHP 8.4.24), not inferred — this is a genuine uncaught PHP Error (fatal), not a warning or a styling/rendering issue.
❌ Problematic Code
`app/design/frontend/Kemana/steelhub/Magento_Sales/templates/order/
view.phtml`, line 27 — the exact call chain: this phtml → rendered
via `Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template::fetchView` →
`AbstractBlock::_toHtml`/`_loadCache` → standard Magento layout
rendering. The debug stack trace (captured directly from the live
error page) confirms this exact file/line as the fatal point.
✅ Fixed Code
Add a null/existence check in `view.phtml` around line 27 before
calling the method on whatever object is null (likely the current
invoice, shipment, or a related order-type resolver) — return early
or render a safe fallback instead of fatally erroring. The real fix
depends on WHY that object is null in the first place (a missing
block argument, a broken DI wiring, or a genuine data issue for
these specific tabs) — needs server-side investigation to find that,
not just a defensive null check as a band-aid.
📋 What To Do
HIGH PRIORITY — this is customer-facing and currently blocks viewing Invoice and Shipment details for every order via My Account, not just a cosmetic issue. Since it renders a full debug/stack-trace page (Ignition), this is also a real information-disclosure risk in its own right (framework internals, file paths, PHP version all exposed to any logged-in customer) — flag that angle separately even from the core Invoice/Shipment-viewing breakage. Check whether Ignition's debug mode is intentionally enabled on this staging environment; if this pattern ever reaches production, it needs a generic error page instead, regardless of the underlying bug also being fixed.

23 - [Negative] Verify submitting a complete review actually records it and shows the moderation-pending message
CONFIRMED REAL DEFECT, found via direct network monitoring, not assumed from the UI alone: clicking the 5th star visibly registers (confirmed via a real class change to "on"), and clicking "Kirim Ulasan" fires a real `POST /review/product/post/id/2153/` that gets a 302 (a normal-looking Magento Post/Redirect/Get success response). But even after that redirect completes AND a full hard page reload, the product's review section never leaves its "not yet written" state — no moderation message, no error, nothing. The submission is silently swallowed somewhere between the 302 and the review actually being persisted/displayed. Written as the correct/expected behavior (a successful submission should show the moderation-pending message), so this fails against the current live implementation.
